newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Moldovan parliament ends stalemate, elects speaker.
newsitem.headline: Moldovan parliament ends stalemate, elects speaker.

text.p: The Moldovan parliament ended a two-month stalemate on Wednesday by electing a new speaker to replace Petru Lucinschi, who became the country's president after winning a December election.
The house elected Dumitru Motpan, leader of the majority Agrarian-Democratic Party, by 55 votes to 21, securing the required simple majority of all members by just two votes.
The Agrarians backed Lucinschi for the presidency after their own party candidate, then prime minister Andrei Sangheli, was knocked out in the first round of presidential voting.

Lucinschi, whose plans for speeding up market reforms had been frustrated by the stalemate in parliament, welcomed the election and called on deputies not to block reforms or turn the house into "a battlefield of empty ambitions".
"Reforms in Moldova should be accelerated," Lucinschi told parliament as he presented some 40 bills he said would create a legislative framework for reforms.
These included a 1997 budget, 1997-1998 privatisation programme, new tax, land and civil law codes, laws on private pension funds and combating organised crime.
Lucinschi proposed that all political parties, including the opposition, sign a cooperation pact.
Motpan said the budget was the most urgent of the series of tasks given to parliament by the president.

The 56-year-old speaker graduated from agricultural college. He ran a Soviet collective farm before being elected to the communist-era Moldovan legislature in 1989. He was re-elected in 1994 and served as a deputy speaker.
